papers.title: Micro-Localization: High-Precision Mobile Robot Localization Using Microscopic Ground Texture
papers.abstract: We demonstrate high-precision global localization using natural ground texture viewed through microscope optics, achieving localization in the tens-of-micrometers regime. For the planar ground texture localization problem considered here, we relate optical magnification and image-space localization uncertainty to physical localization precision. Leveraging this relationship, we then develop a microscope-based localization system that addresses the calibration, camera-modeling, and focus challenges introduced by high-magnification imaging. We evaluate this system across several surface textures using a calibrated precision gantry. Across 1,007 held-out queries per surface, the system localizes every query and achieves translation RMSEs of 28$-$73 $\mu$m. Independent photometric registration agrees with the feature-based localization estimates to within approximately 9 $\mu$m RMSE. We further demonstrate localization on a low-cost mobile robot using the gantry-collected maps, and also show that the system can resolve micrometer-scale displacement caused by thermal expansion. These results show that microscopic natural surface texture can bring mobile localization into a precision regime typically associated with fixed positioning systems.

papers.title: When Plans Change, Remember: Replanning-Guided Visual Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Long-horizon, multi-stage Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies often require visual information that is no longer present in the current observation. Retaining the complete observation history is computationally expensive and highly redundant, motivating selective visual memory. We introduce RePlanMem-VLA (Replanning-Guided Keyframe Memory for VLA), which turns a policy's own plan revisions into an online memory-write signal. Under receding-horizon execution, consecutive action chunks predict some of the same future actions. RePlanMem-VLA treats unusually large disagreement between these temporally aligned predictions as evidence of a task-relevant event. We first compare 35 disagreement measures across single-task autoregressive decoder-only and Flow-Matching Transformers trained from scratch, then validate the selected signals on pretrained OpenVLA-OFT and $\pi_{0.5}$ policies over MIKASA-Robo-VLA tasks. The resulting detectors achieve ROC-AUC of 0.981-0.997. We then use the selected signals in RePlanMem-VLA to trigger updates to a bounded visual memory, with a robot-masked write filter suppressing redundant frames. In the evaluated memory-retention experiments, RePlanMem-VLA preserves task-relevant observations until the later decision point in 100% of episodes. Real-robot replay data further show that event selection and redundancy suppression extend beyond simulation. These results establish plan revision as a policy-internal signal for controlling what a VLA remembers. Website: this https URL .

papers.title: RTISSLAM-3D: Full 6-DoF SLAM With an In-Air 3D Imaging Sonar
papers.abstract: Echolocating bats navigate dense forests using sonar alone, and in-air 3D imaging sonars now capture the entire frontal hemisphere with every pulse. Sonar SLAM, however, has so far been planar: current systems estimate a 2D trajectory and discard the elevation information in the sonar images, an assumption that does not hold on rough and sloped terrain such as a forest floor. In this paper, we introduce RTISSLAM-3D, a novel 6-DoF SLAM system for a wheeled robot that carries an in-air 3D imaging sonar, an IMU and wheel encoders. A CFAR detector on the sphere reduces every sonar image to a sparse set of 3D detections, which we use for a 3D acoustic odometry that models the shape of the sonar beam, for place recognition with polar submap descriptors, and for the verification of loop closures by 3D registration, all combined in a 6-DoF pose graph with attitude factors. We evaluated RTISSLAM-3D on a 545m drive through a forest, with a 3D lidar SLAM as reference. The loop closures reduced the horizontal error of the acoustic odometry from 1.74m to 0.28m, with a height error of 0.12m, and 94.6% of the resulting 3D sonar map lies within 0.3 m of the lidar map.

papers.title: Scaling Online Exploration for Robot Agents
papers.abstract: Robot learning has advanced by scaling demonstration datasets and model capacity; however, deploying a new robot embodiment or task typically necessitates a dedicated teleoperation corpus. The resulting policies remain bounded by their imitation distributions, limiting generalization and continual self-improvement. We introduce RAX (Robot Agent eXploration), an open-source framework for robot agents centered on scaling exploration: enabling agents to improve by acquiring online experience and synthesizing executable programs. In RAX, a general-purpose coding agent generates robot control code, operating without action demonstration data, hand-engineered action primitives, or value-function guidance. Through online exploration, the agent identifies decision sequences that achieve task goals and compiles them into modular programs encapsulating the full perception-planning-control loop. Using RAX, we present a systematic multi-embodiment study on scaling online exploration across precision and long-horizon manipulation tasks using single-arm, bimanual, dexterous, mobile, and humanoid systems in simulation and on real robots. Generalization performance on unseen environments improves consistently as exploration scales. In simulation, RAX outperforms top baseline models by +37.4% on average. On real robots, RAX autonomously learns memory-dependent, articulated, high-precision, deformable, and long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks without human demonstrations, continually improving performance by composing verified skills from prior exploration sessions. As exploration scales, we observe emergent capabilities including active perception, error recovery, safety guardrails, and human-robot collaboration. We open-source RAX as a generalist robot-agent platform in which new robot embodiments are integrated through their APIs alone, without teleoperated data collection or policy training.

papers.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
papers.abstract: GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3) physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5) long-horizon preservation of progress. Second, we study the agentic harness for embodied control. We identify that close-loop coordination between a high-level "System 2" reasoner (i.e., GPT-6-Astra) and a low-level "System 1" controller (e.g., {\pi}0.5) is costly but effective. Third, we examine GPT-6-Astra on real-world deployment. Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints. Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks. We develop a prototype that 1) derives tasks from real-world needs, 2) provides no in-domain demonstrations, and 3) judges agents on a world clock that keeps running while they deliberate. Taken together, our results suggest that GPT-6-Astra has largely crossed the threshold of embodied competence, but not yet that of practical embodied intelligence.

papers.title: Mothership: A Two Tier Autonomous Refuse Collection System for Pedestrian Campuses
papers.abstract: Refuse collection in pedestrian campuses, parks and mixed-use districts remains manual because compaction trucks cannot reach bins located on walkways, courtyards and building service doors. This paper presents Mothership, a two-tier autonomous refuse collection system in which an electric compaction truck (the mothership) carries two low-speed sidewalk robots (RoboCarts) that fetch standard two-wheel bins, deliver them to the truck, return the empty bins to their original positions and re-dock on the truck for charging. The architecture separates responsibilities by scale: the truck performs road driving, compaction, lifting and energy supply, while the carts perform only sidewalk transport and bin grasping. This split removes the lift-and-tip mechanism from the sidewalk vehicle, keeping it light and low, and relaxes cart-to-truck docking tolerance to the +/-100 mm capture window of a standard automated lifter. We describe the system architecture, the bin-handling and docking interfaces, and a mission-planning formulation that decomposes a route into truck stop points and cart tasks. A discrete-event simulation over synthetic campus layouts with 2-16 bins/ha quantifies throughput as a function of bin density, cart count and stop-point radius. A two-cart configuration serves 20-29 bins/h. Throughput is governed by an interaction between cart count and stop-point radius: a single cart performs best with many close stops, whereas three or four carts need wide stops (80 m) to stay busy, reaching 35-49 bins/h at moderate-to-high densities. The best stop radius therefore has to be chosen together with the fleet size, not fixed in advance.

papers.title: DriveWorld3D Evidence Constrained 3D World Modeling and Generative Simulation for Real-World Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Three dimensional modeling for autonomous driving must continuously estimate road geometry, obstacle occupancy, traffic participant behavior, and observational uncertainty under limited computational resources. Existing reconstruction methods can synthesize realistic novel views, but visual fidelity does not sufficiently characterize the geometric reliability required for driving. Generative world models can expand scenarios and predict future observations, yet may introduce content unsupported by measurements. We propose DriveWorld3D, a framework combining temporal video learning, measurement constraints from multiple sensors, and offline generative simulation. Its online component maintains a unified world state comprising road surfaces, volumetric occupancy, dynamic entities, and road relations, while separately representing physical occupancy, observability, and evidence provenance. Action conditioned future prediction and risk sensitive planning connect this representation to driving decisions. Its offline component reconstructs recorded scenes using neural radiance fields or 3D Gaussian Splatting, then expands long tail conditions using generative models while restricting the use of generated content as geometric ground truth. We specify data partitioning, sensor ablations, fault injection, paired closed loop testing, and real to simulation consistency assessment. The central hypothesis is that explicit evidence management can reduce dangerous false free space predictions and occlusion risk within a matched computational budget while retaining acceptable driving efficiency. All performance claims remain subject to experimental validation. papers.title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
papers.abstract: Pretrained VLMs bring rich world knowledge and semantic priors to object-goal navigation, and fine-tuning a VLM into a navigation policy has become a common recipe. Despite this progress, success rates remain low, and it is unclear which capability these fine-tuned policies lack. Our diagnosis identifies goal grounding as the dominant failure. These policies explore well, yet often fail to notice that the goal is already in view or to estimate how far away it is. To address this failure, we ground the goal explicitly. Explicit grounding substantially improves success and reaches state-of-the-art results on six benchmarks across three scene collections. We also correct annotation defects in these benchmarks, so that future methods are evaluated more faithfully. Our analysis on the clean benchmarks shows that, with ground-truth grounding, our policy nearly matches the expert that generated its demonstrations, leaving the headroom in perception rather than policy learning. Our work points to goal grounding as a missing piece of object-goal navigation and offers a simple and effective solution to the task.

papers.title: SparseMax-dSTL: Sound Robustness with Horizon-Independent Gradient Allocation for Temporal Logic Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: A gradient-based solver that enforces a Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specification uses a smooth approximation of its quantitative semantics, the robustness. In safety-critical trajectory optimization, this approximation must have two properties. First, it must be sound, that is, nonnegative only on trajectories that satisfy the specification. Second, at each temporal operator, the weight of its gradient on the violating samples must stay bounded away from zero, however long the horizon. The approximations in use, including the log-sum-exp, its sound variant, and the generalized-mean robustness, do not have both. We introduce lower approximations of the minimum and the maximum whose gradients are sparsemax projections, and we prove that the robustness built from them has both. It lies below the exact robustness and is therefore sound, and its error has a bound that is independent of the number of samples and known before optimization. The gradient of each approximation is exactly zero on every sample beyond a data-dependent threshold, so the weight on violating samples a gap beyond the others has a positive lower bound at every horizon. On a planar unicycle and on a seven-joint manipulator beside a person in simulation, the log-sum-exp approximation is positive on a violating trajectory. As the horizon of the manipulator's task grows from 10 to 80 s, the gradient weight of the sound variant on the violating samples falls from 0.22 to 0.04, while that of sparsemax stays at 1. In a constrained trajectory optimization of the unicycle, the constraint on the log-sum-exp robustness returns a violating trajectory, whereas the constraint on the sparsemax robustness returns a trajectory that satisfies the specification with the required margin.

papers.title: Self-Building Labs
papers.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for. Adapting them to a new experiment still takes extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery. We introduce the self-building laboratory (SBL), which designs, configures, and operates its own laboratory setup given a high-level scientific goal. SBL starts from whatever already exists, from an empty room to a working SDL, and builds the missing capabilities: the lab layout, its digital twin, robot skills, and experimental workflows. We demonstrate the system working across different robots and setups, scaling from a single workstation to laboratories with several robots working together. We validate SBL's end-to-end capabilities through a real-world quantum-dot synthesis experiment. By shifting the role of human researchers from manually configuring and programming device automation to specifying scientific objectives, SBL makes scientific automation more accessible, flexible, and scalable. papers.title: Structural Affinity: An Algorithm for Coherent Cage-Based Shape Design
papers.abstract: Cage-based deformation (CBD) parametrises 3D geometry through a small set of control handles, effectively enabling a variety of tasks from animation and interactive modelling to tool-based co-design, neural deformation transfer, and aerodynamic shape optimization. Many optimization approaches relying on CBD employ regularisation strategies to reduce the distortion of the deformed mesh by encouraging smooth, regular cage deformations. These techniques offer soft guidance to an optimization algorithm towards desirable deformations, but compete with the task objective rather than changing the deformation parameterization itself. In this work we introduce Structural Affinity for CBD, an explicit regularisation method which enables smooth deformations through control cages by exploiting a two-cage structure to couple cage-handle motion directly. Structural Affinity precomputes an affinity matrix using mean-value coordinates, binding the inner control-cage to a coarser outer-cage. This matrix defines how much a cage handle displacement propagates to neighbouring handles which substantially decreases and often eliminates cage self-intersections, reduces mesh distortion, and adds linear overhead at deformation time. Across robotic control--morphology co-design, source-to-target neural deformation transfer, and aerodynamic wing shape optimization, Structural Affinity produces more regular deformations and substantially reduces reliance on hand-designed structural loss terms. We report consistent gains on three complementary diagnostics: the cotangent Laplacian, a proxy for surface smoothness; cage distortion, capturing whether control handles move coherently; and surface roughness, which measures undesirable oscillation in wing geometry.

papers.title: Online Constraint Optimization-Based Indirect-Adaptive Robust Control for Autonomous Vehicles with Unknown Friction
papers.abstract: Friction uncertainty is a significant challenge for autonomous vehicle control, undermining feasibility and performance. This paper proposes a novel two-layer control framework to achieve vehicle motion control under large friction uncertainty by combining optimization-based planning with indirect adaptive robust control (IARC). The upper layer solves a constrained optimal control problem to generate a feasible trajectory that satisfies all the constraints in a time-optimal manner along the desired path. The lower layer, IARC, adapts the unknown parameters related to friction uncertainty and combines model compensation with robust feedback to ensure transient and steady-state tracking performance. An estimation monitor is designed to prevent poor learning when data indicate a model mismatch, while a smooth parameter reset reduces the estimated tire capacity and limits abrupt tightening of constraints. The updated parameters are fed back into the model and constraints in the planner, enabling trajectory replanning as friction conditions change. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method achieves accurate tracking of the desired trajectory and online friction adaptation under large friction uncertainty while ensuring time-optimal vehicle motion. The simulation results demos are available at this https URL .

papers.title: TriSAR-3D and PaintFusion: A Novel Trimodal LiDAR-RGB-Thermal Dataset and Method for 3D Person Detection in Search and Rescue
papers.abstract: Reliable 3D person detection is important for rescue robotics to give first responders situational awareness. Yet most multimodal 3D detection research targets automotive scenarios in which pedestrians mostly appear in a narrow range of upright, near-road poses. It is therefore unclear how much of the reported performance transfers to rescue settings, as a person may be lying, partially occluded, or in unstructured indoor and outdoor environments. To investigate this gap, we introduce TriSAR-3D, a multimodal person detection dataset recorded with a high-resolution 128-channel LiDAR, an RGB camera, and a thermal camera. It captures varied poses in indoor as well as outdoor locations at different times of day to study their influence on 3D object detector performance. Furthermore, we propose a novel trimodal 3D detection pipeline, PaintFusion, that fuses PointPainting-based evidence using a simple MLP. We show that the derived method reaches 65.4 AP@50 and thereby outperforms strong LiDAR-only (CenterPoint, 53.4), RGB+LiDAR (BEVFusion, 60.5), and adapted trimodal (Tri-BEVFusion, 60.7) baselines on the dataset. At the same time, it is substantially faster than other fusion-based methods such as BEVFusion, with a per-frame latency of 51.6 ms compared to 101 ms. Additionally, we test how the performance of different 3D object detectors generalizes to unseen pose categories. Removing lying instances from training data collapses the lying-pose AP@50 to near zero across all evaluated detectors. The results indicate that dataset diversity exerts a large effect on 3D object detection performance. The dataset and code are available at this https URL .

papers.title: EmbodiedMidtrain: Bridging the Gap between Vision-Language Models and Vision-Language-Action Models via Mid-training
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) inherit their visual and linguistic capabilities from Vision-Language Models (VLMs), yet most VLAs are built from off-the-shelf VLMs that are not adapted to the embodied domain, limiting their downstream performance. In this work, we propose EmbodiedMidtrain to bridge the gap between VLMs and VLAs. We first characterize the data distribution gap between them, showing that VLA data occupy compact regions that are largely separated from the broader VLM distribution, while the degree of alignment varies substantially both across and within VLM data sources. Then, we build a mid-training data engine that leverages a lightweight learnable proximity estimator to select the most VLA-aligned candidates from a large VLM pool, and produce EmbodiedMidtrain-1M, a VLM dataset that we further use to mid-train the VLM before downstream VLA fine-tuning. Experiments on both simulated robot manipulation benchmarks and real-world tasks show consistent VLA performance gains over off-the-shelf checkpoints across VLM backbones and VLA action heads. These gains extend to downstream tasks not used to guide data selection. Further analysis reveals that mid-training provides a stronger initialization for VLA fine-tuning, with gains emerging from the earliest steps and widening throughout training. Moreover, the data engine captures both dataset-level and sample-level alignment signals, favoring spatial reasoning over text-centric tasks while preserving the diversity of the VLM data. We will release all code, data and models for future research.

executive_summary: New proprioception- and touch-centric methods substantially improve contact-rich and blind manipulation, from peg-in-hole assembly to dexterous Baoding ball rotation.

Foundation-model-driven perception and spatial memory are being tightly integrated with mobile manipulators and VLN agents for more robust navigation and rearrangement under occlusion and body constraints.
Multiple works advance world and dynamics modeling for planning, including object-centric rigid 3D world models, neural time fields, and structured off-road dynamics for aggressive navigation.

Generalist VLA/WAM ecosystems are rapidly maturing, with new frameworks for multi-arm coordination, long-horizon language-guided manipulation, event-triggered memory, and efficient or transferable action experts.

RL and control advances target safer, more sample-efficient planning and control, from sparsemax STL robustness and metareasoning about compute budgets to whole-body loco-manipulation and adaptive vehicle control.
Mapping, localization, and SLAM see notable progress, including microscopic-precision localization, sonar-based full 6-DoF SLAM, and dynamic-scene SLAM leveraging motion-derived uncertainty.

institution_matches.title: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts
institution_matches.overview: Demonstrates blind, contact-rich assembly policies that rely solely on joint proprioception, without vision or tactile/force sensing. RL-trained in simulation over many randomized assemblies, the policies transfer zero-shot to real robots, achieving 73% success on diverse peg insertions and generalizing better to unseen parts than matched visual policies.

institution_matches.title: Foundation-Model-Driven 3D Scene Graphs for Mobile Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: Integrates a foundation-model-driven 3D scene-graph system (FOUND-IT) into a mobile manipulator to serve as spatial memory for navigation and manipulation. On-robot experiments show support for change detection, multi-session mapping, path determination, and direct grasp execution for scene rearrangement, along with a detailed analysis of monocular 3D scene-graph limitations.

institution_matches.title: Ego2Contact: Predicting Touch from Egocentric Human Video for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: Learns a visual–tactile prior from human egocentric video and transfers it to robot hands to predict dense bimanual contact fields from RGB alone. The predictor, aligned via anatomical region correspondences, outperforms prior tactile predictors and enables policies that recover part of the performance of true tactile sensing in both simulated RL and real-robot post-training.

institution_matches.title: Structured Perception Representations for Off-road Dynamics Learning
institution_matches.overview: Introduces SpatialBEV, which conditions off-road vehicle dynamics on local bird's-eye-view perception features queried around predicted states. Across seasonal datasets and high-speed hardware trials, it cuts prediction error by 17.1% and maximum cross-track error by 25.3% compared to physics-based and learned baselines, improving aggressive off-road navigation.

institution_matches.title: What Makes a Good Symbol for Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Planning?
institution_matches.overview: Defines "solver-sufficient" symbolic abstractions that expose the discrete commitments needed for efficient hybrid planning and proposes a counterexample-guided symbol-invention algorithm. Extends the concept to neural energy-based objectives, showing learned symbols can cut solving cost while preserving solution quality and improving interpretability in simulated and real-robot tasks.

institution_matches.title: FCTS: Failure-Guided Curriculum Tree Search Over Generated Terrain for Legged Parkour
institution_matches.overview: Presents a failure-conditioned terrain curriculum that synthesizes new training terrains directly from localized traversal failures for quadruped parkour. Using MCTS to explore curriculum trees under a fixed budget, it boosts success from 28.4% to 85.8% on medium and 14.9% to 44.7% on hard construction-site courses, with demonstrated real-world transfer.

institution_matches.title: Embodiment-Classifier Guidance: Transferring Frozen VLAs Across Robot Dynamics without Demonstrations
institution_matches.overview: Adapts a frozen flow-matching VLA ($\pi_0$) to new robot embodiments using a lightweight embodiment classifier trained on a few calibration tasks, without new demonstrations or policy updates. Classifier gradients guide each denoising step toward target-body-successful actions, yielding a 31% relative reduction in failures across 12 LIBERO suite–controller pairs and suggesting a promising sim-to-real transfer mechanism.

institution_matches.title: EmbodiedMidtrain: Bridging the Gap between Vision-Language Models and Vision-Language-Action Models via Mid-training
institution_matches.overview: Quantifies the distribution gap between generic VLM data and VLA training data, then introduces a mid-training data engine to select VLA-aligned VLM samples and mid-train the backbone before action fine-tuning. Across multiple VLMs and VLA heads, this mid-training consistently improves manipulation and navigation performance, including on tasks not used to select the data.

topic_matches.title: TransNav: Transformer-Based End-to-End Navigation Method for Static and Dynamic Quadrotor Obstacle Avoidance
topic_matches.overview: Proposes TransNav, an end-to-end transformer policy for quadrotor navigation that encodes point clouds into compact patch features and directly predicts finite-horizon action sequences. An unsupervised training scheme optimizes trajectory-level costs through a point-mass dynamics model, yielding strong obstacle avoidance in dense static and dynamic environments with low onboard inference cost.

topic_matches.title: Embodiment-Aware Planning for Heterogeneous Bimanual Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: Formulates execution of a single human-demonstrated object motion on a dual-arm robot with heterogeneous grippers (e.g., suction and parallel-jaw) as a finite-horizon optimization over arm-trajectory and handover assignments. The planner reasons over grasp feasibility, constraints, manipulability, and switching regularization, enabling tasks that are infeasible for any single gripper alone.

topic_matches.title: Reinforcement Learning Based Multi-Terrain Adaptive Whole-Body Control for a Quadruped Manipulator
topic_matches.overview: Introduces a reinforcement-learning whole-body control framework for a small quadruped equipped with a manipulator, coordinating locomotion and end-effector tasks via a hybrid task representation and task-prioritized learning. Real-world trials on slopes, stairs, and deformable terrain show terrain-adaptive loco-manipulation while maintaining task-consistent end-effector behavior.

topic_matches.title: No Eyes, No Problem: What Does Touch Contribute to Blind Baoding Ball Manipulation?
topic_matches.overview: Studies blind in-hand Baoding ball manipulation on a Shadow Dexterous Hand Lite using only proprioception and binary tactile feedback, with RL policies trained in carefully randomized simulation. Through embodiment-aligned sim design and novel domain randomizations, the policy transfers zero-shot and achieves 225 consecutive 180° rotations without vision, setting a new hardware benchmark.

topic_matches.title: SimpleVLN: Towards Simple and Frontier Vision-Language Navigation
topic_matches.overview: Shows that native multimodal LLMs can perform strong vision–language navigation when paired with an architecture-preserving framework that uses fixed-budget global–local memory and action chunking. A progressive IL–DAgger–RL pipeline and large-scale synthesized tasks enable success rates up to 80.1% on RxR-CE, surpassing prior VLN methods without task-specific model changes.

topic_matches.title: ORD-WM: Learning Object-Centric Rigid Dynamics for 3D World Modeling in Robotic Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: Proposes an object-centric 3D world model where a vector-neuron VAE encodes each rigid object and an action-conditioned dynamics module predicts object-wise SE(3) increments. By analytically applying predicted rigid transforms rather than regenerating latents, ORD-WM preserves geometry over long rollouts and supports real-time MPC replanning in simulated and real manipulation.

topic_matches.title: BeJEPA: A Goal-Conditioned Humanoid Behavior World Model via Unsupervised RL
topic_matches.overview: Introduces BeJEPA, a JEPA-based world-action model that jointly embeds humanoid posture and world pose, with separate dynamic and successor predictors for one-step physical grounding and long-horizon goal conditioning. It significantly reduces global position error in 20 s tracking tasks and enables a Unitree G1 to attain posture and world-heading goals with disturbance recovery.

topic_matches.title: GRASP: Global-Local Representation Alignment and Spatial-Physical Grounding for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
topic_matches.institution: Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong SAR, China.; OWARobot Co. Ltd; Robot Co. Ltd, China.; WARobot Co. Ltd, China.; WARobot Co. Ltd, China. ffiliation:
topic_matches.overview: Presents GRASP, a VLA framework for bimanual manipulation that injects physics-grounded priors via differentiable forward kinematics in the loss and distills global and local visual queries from DINO teachers. The resulting joint-space flow policy better aligns errors with task-space consequences and focuses attention on hand–object regions, improving long-horizon bimanual performance in sim and on hardware.

topic_matches.title: Bio-Inspired Magnetic Navigation Using Gradient Descent With Rao-Blackwellized Particle Filtering
topic_matches.overview: Proposes a bio-inspired magnetic navigation method that forgoes pre-built magnetic maps, instead estimating local field gradients via a Rao-Blackwellized particle filter and following them to the goal. This yields a simple, memory-efficient navigation strategy suitable for GPS-denied environments where conventional magnetic mapping is impractical.

topic_matches.title: VLA-Fabric: Learning Interaction for Composable Multi-Arm VLA Agents
topic_matches.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
topic_matches.overview: Introduces VLA-Fabric, which composes one full VLA policy per arm and enables explicit inter-policy interaction at shared-context, latent, and action stages. Experiments with 3–4-arm teams in simulation and on real robots show 16–40 percentage point gains over independently trained local policies, indicating that learned VLA-to-VLA coordination scales multi-arm manipulation.
